name: Question 15
worked_solution:
Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that 

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-{e}^{-x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(-{e}^{-x})\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-{e}^{-x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(-{e}^{-x})\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-I.\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+J \\ I & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-I) \\ I & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-I \\ 2I & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{e}^{-x}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =(\frac{{e}^{-x}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{-\pi }}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ))-(\frac{{e}^{\pi }}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-\pi }}{2}-\frac{{e}^{\pi }}{2} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-\pi }-{e}^{\pi }}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15

Evaluate ∫−ππe−xcos⁡xdx.

a
 eπ+e−π4
b
 1−e−2π2
c
 −e−π+2eπ2
d
 e−π−eπ2
e
 e2π−14
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's denote the indefinite integral by I=∫e−xcos⁡xdx.

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that u=e−x⇒dudx=−e−x,dvdx=cos⁡x⇒v=∫cos⁡xdx=sin⁡x.

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get I=∫e−xcos⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=e−x(sin⁡x)−∫(sin⁡x)(−e−x)dx=e−xsin⁡x+∫e−xsin⁡xdx=e−xsin⁡x+J.

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate J=∫e−xsin⁡xdx.

To do this, let's suppose that u=e−x⇒dudx=−e−x,dvdx=sin⁡x⇒v=∫sin⁡xdx=−cos⁡x.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get J=∫e−xsin⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=e−x(−cos⁡x)−∫(−cos⁡x)(−e−x)dx=−e−xcos⁡x−∫e−xcos⁡xdx=−e−xcos⁡x−I.

So, substituting this into our equation for I, we can subsequently solve for I: I=e−xsin⁡x+JI=e−xsin⁡x+(−e−xcos⁡x−I)I=e−xsin⁡x−e−xcos⁡x−I2I=e−xsin⁡x−e−xcos⁡xI=e−x2(sin⁡x−cos⁡x)

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows: ∫−ππe−xcos⁡xdx=(e−x2(sin⁡x−cos⁡x))|−ππ=(e−π2(sin⁡π−cos⁡π))−(eπ2(sin⁡(−π)−cos⁡(−π)))=e−π2−eπ2=e−π−eπ2
